scientific_queries.note: Cross-task transfer test of the R37 budget rule; no novelty claim.

subagent_note: None dispatched: the result is a decisive non-transfer with a stated moderator, and the confound between task and prediction strength is disclosed.

design.task: BATCHIE high-diversity design: 37 compound one-hot features, train 100 / pool 251 per unit
design.hit_definition: selected pair in the true bottom quartile of the pool (chance 25%)

moderator: prediction strength: GDSC's point prediction comes from pathway/tissue annotation (rho about 0.20) and the mix helps at large k; BATCHIE's comes from compound identity (rho about 0.94) and pure exploitation wins at every k
correction_to_C28: the budget boundary is not a universal rule; it holds only when the point prediction is weak. The corrected statement is more useful because prediction strength can be checked before deployment.
consistency_with_C19: C19 says the bulk is additive and the tail is not: deciding whether a pair is in the bottom quartile is easy (97% here) while deciding which pair is best is hard (R23 precision@10 0.225)
confound_disclosed: prediction strength and task are not fully separable in this comparison, because the two tasks also differ in feature type and hit definition

register_updates.C28: premise added (only when the point prediction is weak)
register_updates.C32: new and refuted: the decision rule does not transfer across tasks

next_gates: manipulate prediction strength WITHIN one task (GDSC with tissue-only vs tissue+pathway features) to test the moderator rather than observe it
